_comment: Scan self-checks for the NAILS forensic oracle. The positive controls are three reserved @oracle.example addresses that the pipeline (ci/oracle/make-sample-images.sh) writes into the unallocated space past the end of the 'after' image's filesystem, a region no file covers and that before/control leave zero, so no file, path or record changes and only the carved address is new. bulk_extractor reads the whole image, unallocated space included, and carves each address with no format-aware parser, at the exact (bulk_extractor, email, <address>) key these controls pin. A control counts as detected only when 'after' carries it and before and control do not: if one is missing or already in the baseline the scan is blind and the run fails (never 'clean'), because a scan that cannot see a record it should cannot be trusted to report no residue. This proves the channel that reads unallocated space sees a string planted there, the class a leaked-then-deleted trace falls in; it does not prove a format-aware parser understood a record. The canary is a reserved address planted on every image at an otherwise-uncovered path; finding it proves the scan read the image's contents. The scan may rotate the canary per run (ORACLE_SEED) and pins whatever it planted in a run-time copy of this file; the value below is the default used when nothing rotates it. 'tool' pins the channel that must surface a check; 'path' and 'field' locate it (a bulk_extractor feature type and its exact value). Keep these in step with what make-sample-images.sh plants.

positive_controls.name: unallocated-1
positive_controls.note: Written into the unallocated space past the end of the 'after' image's filesystem.
